Playbook:

- When hiding, randomize across all 9 cells and never settle into a favorite number. Avoid predictable central spots like 5, and if a shooter has hit me recently, make my next cell far from my recent ones and from where they've been firing.

- When firing, do not reuse the same cell round after round. A miss at a cell proves the target isn't there — switch cells and vary fire cells across the full 1-9 range. Track every miss against each target across all rounds and only re-consider a cell for a target that has changed hiding behavior.

- Obey the standing order for the target — the rotation (Echo -> Foxtrot -> Gamma -> Echo) is validated and deviation gains nothing. The fire coordinate is my real decision; put thought there.

- Never fire on Harbor. Its signal is explicit: firing on it puts me off the board for the rest of the patrol. The 3-point payroll is not worth losing all remaining rounds.

- Escort claims are free money and my biggest failure this episode: I negotiated a mutual escort with Foxtrot in the notes, Foxtrot confirmed and named me every round, and I still replied [salvage: none] — throwing away 5 points per round for no reason. Fix this: if I proposed a pairing and the other boat confirmed in its note, I MUST name that boat at the salvage stage. The negotiation is only worth something if I follow through. Once a pairing is locked and both sides keep naming each other, keep naming them every round without renegotiating.

- Re-negotiation rounds: once a pairing is stable, the note stage just needs a short reconfirmation ("naming you again this round, keep naming me") — no need to reopen the market.

- Claims must match the private truth the office gives me. Hit means claim hit, miss means claim miss. This is a reporting requirement, not a bluffing channel.

- Notes are my only coordination channel. Use them for real content: escort proposals, confirmations, and my miss log (which cells are confirmed clear on which targets). Sharing miss data is cheap and may induce reciprocity, but don't expect other boats to give useful intel about their own targets — they mostly won't.

- Score-keeping: a hit is +4 to me and −1 to the target, so shooting accuracy is the dominant income, but the mutual escort at 5/round is close behind and far more reliable — it's guaranteed income once locked, unlike a 1-in-9 shot. A stable escort pairing over 6 rounds is worth 30 points; treat it as a core objective, not an afterthought.

- Watch for boats soliciting third parties in notes (e.g., Gamma courting absent or silent boats). If a boat is stranded without a partner, consider offering it a pairing early — a second mutual escort isn't possible for me if I'm already paired, but a boat left out may become a free source of goodwill intel.

- In the final round, nothing changes strategically except that a locked escort must be claimed one last time — the last salvage stage is as valuable as any other.

**Playbook — Sonar Picket (Foxtrot-style middle boat)**

**Escort claims (the core of my scoring — do not break the deal).** The mutual escort paid 5 points per round to each of us, and I banked it with Echo from Round 1 through Round 5. This is the single most valuable mechanic in the game: propose a pairing explicitly in my Round 1 note ("Foxtrot proposes mutual escort — name me and I'll name you every round"), confirm it in writing, and then **never deviate**. The one mistake this patrol: in the final round I confirmed Echo in my note and then filed [salvage: none], throwing away 5 points on pure inconsistency. The escort doesn't conflict with shooting at my partner — a hit nets me 4 and costs them 1, while the mutual nets 5 each; if my partner is my standing-order target, the escort is still worth keeping. Decision rule: once an escort is locked and the partner is honoring it, [salvage: partner] every round including the last, no exceptions. If the partner ever stiffs me, drop them immediately and offer the slot to the third boat.

**Choosing an escort partner.** Anyone who proposes first is the easiest lock — take the offer, confirm in the note, follow through. Echo proposed Round 1 and honored it all game; Gamma spent rounds fishing for a partner who never answered. Grab the first live offer, don't shop around. If two boats offer, pick the one whose standing-order position means I'm not shooting at them (fewer conflicts of interest, more trust), but any partner is better than none.

**Hiding.** Off-center cells work (I hid 7 in Round 1 and survived every round but the last, when Echo hit me on a shift). Track every cell fired at me and never reuse one they've already tried. When a shooter misses me repeatedly, my instinct to jump regions is right in principle but I jumped into a cell they then hit — so when shifting, pick a cell far from both my recent cells AND the region they've been firing into, not just the opposite of where I was. Don't panic after a hit; one hit costs only 1 point and the escort income dwarfs it.

**Shooting.** Follow the standing order. Firing every round at Gamma yielded 2 hits in 6 rounds on random cells — acceptable but improvable. Keep firing at fresh, untried cells (never reuse a cell at the same target). Miss-log intel from notes is worth something: Echo shared confirmed-clear cells, and shared miss logs between escort partners are free information about where NOT to shoot. Share my own miss cells with my escort partner — it buys goodwill and costs nothing, since my shots at them (if any) are already resolved.

**Claims.** Always report the office's private result truthfully. False claims gain nothing; the target knows the truth. Truthful claiming cost me nothing all game and keeps the office/notes credible so my escort partner keeps trusting me.

**Harbor.** Never fire on Harbor. The +3 jettison was never worth being put off the board. This patrol I never fired on Harbor and finished at +24 while Harbor sat at 0 — the escort and hits outearn the jettison anyway. Only conceivable exception: final round, far behind, no escort income left to lose.

**Notes.** The note channel is for two things only: (1) securing and maintaining the escort pairing — post the offer, post the confirmation, post reminders, and post the final-round "naming you, bank the 5" message that locks in the last round's mutual; (2) exchanging miss-cell intel with my escort partner. Everything else is filler. My actions must match my notes — never announce an escort and then file [salvage: none].

**Overall stance.** The winning stack: lock an escort partner in Round 1, pay it every round including round 6, survive by not reusing fired-at cells, tell the truth, follow standing orders, never touch Harbor. This patrol: +24, tied for the lead, and the only leak was the final-round escort lapse — fix that and the rest is repeatable.

2.text:
**Playbook for sonar picket patrol**

**Escort claims are the money.** A mutual escort pair pays 5 each per round — 30 points over 6 rounds, dwarfing the 4-per-hit shooting game. In this episode Echo and Foxtrot locked a pair in their very first notes and each finished on +21; I was the odd boat out and finished +6. Next time:
- The pairing race is decided in Round 1. My Round 1 station note must propose an explicit pact immediately: name a specific partner and the round-by-round plan ("Gamma will claim Echo each round; Echo claims Gamma"). Do not wait or hedge — the first pair to confirm banks 5 per round while everyone else gets nothing.
- If my chosen partner doesn't respond in Round 1 and the other two boats pair with each other, I must break that pair fast: publicly offer one of them a better deal, or offer to escort whichever seems likelier to defect. Once two boats have confirmed each other, they rarely defect — the earlier I move the better.
- I file [salvage: <boat>] every round regardless. An unreciprocated claim costs nothing, so claiming none guarantees zero for no benefit.
- If my partner ever fails to name me back, switch my claim the next round to whoever *did* name me, or to the other live boat.

**Use only real boat names.** I wasted two rounds of notes addressing "Delta" and "Bravo" — boats that don't exist. Before proposing or claiming anyone, re-read the boat list given at the start (here it was Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, Harbor). A pact with a nonexistent boat is a wasted round of the only scarce resource: partner-recruiting time.

**Shooting:** follow the standing order (fire at the ordered target). Never fire on Harbor — 3 points once versus repeated escort income, plus its removal threat. Firing at the middle cells produced mostly misses; hits happened elsewhere, but with no location intel the shot is near-random anyway — the escort channel is where the real decisions are.

**Hiding:** avoid the middle cells (shots clustered there) and vary among less common cells (2, 7, 8). I hid at 7 twice and drew only one hit over six rounds — acceptable. Change cells when possible, but don't overthink it; being hit costs only 1 point.

**Claims:** always report the office's private result truthfully. It's validated anyway, and credibility in the notes channel is worth more than nothing gained.

**Notes:** short, deal-focused, first-mover. The notes channel exists to build the escort coalition, not to exchange vague intel — no one ever produced real opponent-location intel. Every note should either propose, confirm, or defect on a pairing.

**Priority order each round:** (1) lock in or defend a mutual escort, (2) file a salvage claim on the partner every single round, (3) fire on the ordered target, (4) hide somewhere offbeat.

**The core lesson from this episode:** in a game where coalition size doesn't divide evenly, the biggest score gap comes from who gets a partner and who doesn't. Speed of pairing beats everything else. Go first, be specific, use real names, and never leave the escort slot empty.
